strings.name: Sanae Takaichi
strings.summary: A Kobe graduate trained at the Matsushita Institute, Takaichi entered parliament in 1993. She held senior LDP roles and portfolios including internal affairs and economic security. Japan’s first female prime minister from 2025, she was designated again in 2026. Her economic, defense and conservative historical positions attract support and controversy.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Her long participation in Japan’s cabinet and ruling party shapes debate on economic security, technology and national identity.

strings.highlights.h1.title: First female prime minister
strings.highlights.h1.text: Her 2025 designation broke Japan’s premiership gender barrier.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Economic security policy
strings.highlights.h2.text: Held cabinet responsibility for economic security and technology matters.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Designated again

strings.timeline.t2.text: Succeeded Ishiba as Japan’s first female prime minister.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Economic security portfolio

strings.timeline.t4.title: Internal affairs minister

strings.timeline.t5.text: Held portfolios including Okinawa, Northern Territories and science policy.
